div.head: Wl Lond 2
div.ab: ⁊ ic kyðe eoƿ, þæt ic ƿylle, þæt get beon eallra þæra laga ƿeorðe, þe gyt ƿæran on Eadƿerdes dæge kynges.
Et ego uobis notum facio, quod ego uolo, quod uos sitis omni lege illa digni, qua fuistis Edwardi diebus regis.
7 ic kyðe eow þæt ic wylle þæt get beon eallra þæra laga weorðe þe gyt wæran on Eadwurdes dæge kynges.
2. Und ich künde euch, dass ich will, dass ihr beide aller der Rechte theilhaft seiet, derer ihr beide zu König Eadwards [III.] Lebzeiten [theilhaft] waret.
2. And I make known to you that I will that you both be partakers of all the rights of which you both were [partakers] in King Eadward's [III.] lifetime.
I declare to you that it is my will that both of you shall be entitled to all the rights which you had in the time of King Edward.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 230–231 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 486, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: Bistum und Stadt. Dual lebt bis um 1200
Bishopric and city. The dual survives until c. 1200

Nicht etwa neuen Status der Freien (im Ggs. zu früherer Unfreiheit) oder der Gerichts- und Eidesfähigkeit verleiht Wilhelm [gegen Norton Comment. on Lond. 258. 264f.], sondern er bestätigt ‘franchises’; Stubbs Lect. Engl. hist. 122

What William confers is not, say, a new status of freemen (as opposed to former unfreedom), or the capacity to appear in court and to swear oaths [against Norton Comment. on Lond. 258. 264f.]; rather, he confirms ‘franchises’; Stubbs Lect. Engl. hist. 122
Harold II. (s. d. Gl) wird vom Normannischen Hofe als ungesetzlicher Herrscher übergangen
Harold II (see that word in Gl) is passed over by the Norman court as an unlawful ruler
